cohort: 90 primiparous singleton pregnant women, 30 of whom had undergone bariatric surgery 1-5 years prior and 60 of whom had a BMI ≥ 30 kg/m(2)
finding: Bariatric surgery was associated with lower rates of fetal macrosomia, gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, and cesarean section, but higher rates of SGA, PTD, and cholestasis, compared to obesity.
